questions.prompt: Which popular sweet, shaped like small round balls, is shared across India during Diwali?
questions.explain: Ladoo is the most popular sweet made from flour, sugar, and ghee, gifted to friends and family during Diwali!

questions.prompt: Which famous festival in India is known as the "Festival of Colours"?
questions.explain: During Holi, people throw vibrant coloured powders (gulal) and water at each other to welcome spring!

questions.prompt: During the Uttarayan festival in Gujarat, what fills the sky in thousands of bright colours?
questions.explain: Uttarayan is the famous kite-flying festival where everyone goes up to their rooftops to fly colourful kites!

questions.prompt: What main sweet dish made of rice, milk, and sugar/jaggery is cooked during the harvest festival of Pongal?
questions.explain: Pongal is cooked in a traditional pot until it boils over, symbolizing abundance and prosperity!

questions.prompt: Which delicious, spiced rice dish layered with meat or veggies is a favorite feast during Eid in India?
questions.explain: Biryani is a fragrant, festive rice dish cooked with spices and herbs, enjoyed during celebrations!

questions.prompt: What is the popular energetic circular group dance performed during the 9 nights of Navratri in Gujarat?
questions.explain: Garba is a joyful Gujarati dance where people dress in colorful clothes and dance in concentric circles!

questions.prompt: What do people light in and around their homes during Diwali, the "Festival of Lights"?
questions.explain: Diyas (earthen oil lamps) are lit all around houses during Diwali to welcome positivity, light, and good fortune!

questions.prompt: Which refreshing yogurt-based drink, served either sweet or salted, is loved all across India?
questions.explain: Lassi is a smooth, chilled yogurt drink that is super refreshing, especially in warm weather!

questions.prompt: What is the most famous street food in Mauritius, made of a thin flatbread filled with yellow split peas?
questions.explain: Dholl Puri is Mauritius's favorite street snack — warm flatbread stuffed with ground split peas, served with tasty curries!

questions.prompt: Which tropical sweet cake made from sweet potato and coconut is made in Mauritius during Diwali?
questions.explain: Gateau Patate is a delicious local Mauritian sweet pastry stuffed with coconut and sugar!

questions.prompt: What tasty tomato-based stew with garlic and herbs is a comfort food served over rice in Mauritian homes?
questions.explain: Rougaille is a rich Creole tomato sauce cooked with spices and herbs, eaten with rice or bread.

questions.prompt: During the festival of Maha Shivaratri, thousands of people in Mauritius walk to which sacred lake?
questions.explain: Grand Bassin is a peaceful crater lake surrounded by temples where pilgrims gather every year.

questions.prompt: Which annual festival in Mauritius celebrates island culture, music, Sega dance, and food?
questions.explain: The Kreol Festival is a week of vibrant music, arts, and island celebrations loved by everyone!

questions.prompt: Which colorful festival is celebrated in Mauritius with lion dances, red envelopes, and fireworks?
questions.explain: Chinese New Year is a major public holiday in Mauritius, filled with lion dances and festive food!

questions.prompt: What delicious pickled fish or vegetable dish cooked with mustard seeds is a Mauritian favorite?
questions.explain: Vindaye is a flavorful dish seasoned with mustard, turmeric, garlic, and chilies.

questions.prompt: Which fresh fruit is often sprinkled with chili powder and salt as a delicious beach street snack in Mauritius?
questions.explain: Juicy pineapple or mango slices coated with chili and salt are popular tropical snacks sold along Mauritian beaches!

questions.prompt: How do you say a friendly "Hello / Good morning" in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "Bonzur" is the warm everyday greeting used across Mauritius!

questions.prompt: How do you say "Thank you" in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "Mersi" is the simple way to say thank you in Creole.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Good evening" in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "Bonswa" is used when greeting someone in the evening.

questions.prompt: What does the super common Creole phrase "Ki manyer?" mean when greeting a friend?
questions.explain: "Ki manyer?" means "How are you doing?" or "How's it going?"

questions.prompt: How do you say "Please" politely in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "Silvouplé" is used when asking for something politely.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Sorry / Excuse me" in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "Padon" is used to apologize or get someone's attention.

questions.prompt: What does the famous island expression "Ayo!" mean in Mauritius?
options: An exclamation of surprise or emotion
questions.explain: "Ayo!" is a fun, universal island expression used when surprised, shocked, or laughing!

questions.prompt: How do you say "Goodbye / See you later" in Mauritian Creole?
questions.explain: "A pli tard" means "See you later" when saying goodbye!

questions.prompt: How do you ask "How are you?" in Gujarati?
questions.explain: "Kem cho?" is the iconic Gujarati phrase to ask someone how they are doing!

questions.prompt: What is the cheerful Gujarati reply to "Kem cho?", meaning "I am doing great!"?
questions.explain: "Maja ma!" means "I'm having fun / All good!"

questions.prompt: What is the warm Gujarati way to say "Goodbye", which literally means "Please come again"?
questions.explain: "Aavjo" means goodbye, but carries the sweet meaning of inviting the person to return!

questions.prompt: How do you ask "What is your name?" in Gujarati?
questions.explain: "Tamaru naam shu che?" is how you politely ask someone's name in Gujarati.

questions.prompt: What is the polite Gujarati word for "Thank you"?
questions.explain: "Dhanyavaad" is used to express heartfelt gratitude.

questions.prompt: What does the Gujarati phrase "Saachu che?" mean when someone tells you interesting news?
questions.explain: "Saachu che?" is used when confirming if something is really true!

questions.prompt: What does the phrase "Barabar che" mean when agreeing with someone in Gujarati?
questions.explain: "Barabar che" means "Everything is fine / Perfect / Correct!"

questions.prompt: Which famous Indian greeting with folded hands means "I bow to the goodness in you"?
questions.explain: "Namaste" is the respectful greeting used all across India with folded hands.

questions.prompt: What colorful flared skirt and blouse outfit is worn by women in Gujarat for Navratri dancing?
questions.explain: Chaniya Choli is a bright, beautiful outfit decorated with mirrors and embroidery!

questions.prompt: What famous tie-dye fabric featuring small dot patterns is crafted in Gujarat and Rajasthan?
questions.explain: Bandhani is made by tying tiny knots in fabric before dyeing it to create patterns!

questions.prompt: What traditional unstitched garment, about 5 to 6 meters long, is gracefully draped by women in India?
questions.explain: The Saree is one of the world's oldest continuous fashion traditions, draped in many styles!

questions.prompt: What natural plant paste is applied in beautiful patterns on hands during weddings and festivals?
questions.explain: Mehndi (Henna) leaves a rich reddish stain on skin and is a symbol of joy and celebration!

questions.prompt: What bright yellow spice paste is applied to the bride and groom before a wedding for glowing skin?
questions.explain: The Haldi ceremony is a fun pre-wedding ritual where family applies yellow turmeric paste to the couple!

questions.prompt: What embroidered leather shoes with stylish curved toes are traditional in Gujarat & Rajasthan?
questions.explain: Mojari are handcrafted leather shoes decorated with colorful embroidery and mirror work.

questions.prompt: What special necklace of black and gold beads is worn by married women in Hindu tradition?
questions.explain: The Mangalsutra is a sacred necklace tied during the wedding ceremony symbolizing love and commitment.

questions.prompt: What long comfortable tunic paired with trousers is worn by both men and women across India?
questions.explain: The Kurta is a versatile, lightweight tunic worn for both daily wear and special occasions.

questions.prompt: What bright traditional headscarf is worn by Creole women in Mauritius during celebrations?
questions.explain: The Mokoto is a colorful headscarf tied elegantly as a proud cultural symbol.

questions.prompt: What lively national dance of Mauritius is performed to drumbeats with rhythmic movements?
questions.explain: Sega is the joyful musical heartbeat of Mauritius that gets everyone dancing!

questions.prompt: Which large round goatskin drum creates the main rhythmic beat for Sega music in Mauritius?
questions.explain: The Ravanne is a circular frame drum warmed over fire to tighten its skin before playing.

questions.prompt: What simple, peaceful color do pilgrims traditionally wear during the Maha Shivaratri walk in Mauritius?
questions.explain: Pilgrims wear simple white clothes as a symbol of peace, purity, and unity.

questions.prompt: What famous handcrafted souvenir from Mauritius is crafted inside glass bottles?
questions.explain: Mauritian artisans are world-renowned for building tiny detailed sailing ships inside glass bottles!

questions.prompt: What traditional outfit brought from India is worn by many Mauritian women at temple festivals?
questions.explain: The Saree remains a cherished traditional outfit for festive and religious events in Mauritius.

questions.prompt: What shaker instrument made from dried sugarcane stalks and seeds is played in Sega music?
questions.explain: The Maravanne is a flat box shaker filled with seeds that adds a rhythmic rustling sound to Sega music.

questions.prompt: What fragrant tropical flower garland is often given to welcome visitors to Mauritius?
questions.explain: Fresh frangipani blossoms are used to welcome guests with tropical island warmth!

questions.prompt: In which year did India celebrate its independence from British rule?
questions.explain: India gained independence on August 15, 1947!

questions.prompt: Which inspiring leader is revered as the "Father of the Nation" in India?
questions.explain: Mahatma Gandhi led India's non-violent freedom movement and inspired peace movements worldwide.

questions.prompt: India is the birthplace of four major religions: Hinduism, Buddhism, Sikhism, and which other?
questions.explain: Jainism, with its philosophy of non-violence and truth, originated in India.

questions.prompt: What famous symbol featuring four standing lions is the National Emblem of India?
questions.explain: The Lion Capital represents strength, courage, and truth.

questions.prompt: How many official languages are recognized in India's Constitution?
questions.explain: India recognizes 22 official languages, celebrating its rich linguistic diversity!

questions.prompt: What symbol in the center of India's national flag represents motion, progress, and law?
questions.explain: The navy blue Ashoka Chakra wheel has 24 spokes representing continuous progress.

questions.prompt: Which major city in Gujarat is home to Mahatma Gandhi's historic Sabarmati Ashram?
questions.explain: Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad was Gandhi's home and the center of the freedom movement.

questions.prompt: What is India's global rank in population size today?
questions.explain: India is currently the most populous nation in the world with over 1.4 billion people!

questions.prompt: Which famous unique flightless bird, now an emblem of extinction, once lived only in Mauritius?
questions.explain: The friendly Dodo bird lived peacefully in Mauritius before human arrivals in the 1600s.

questions.prompt: Which European nation first named and settled the island of Mauritius in 1598?
questions.explain: The Dutch named the island "Mauritius" after Prince Maurice of Nassau!

questions.prompt: What historic UNESCO site in Port Louis marks where Indian workers first arrived in Mauritius?
questions.explain: Aapravasi Ghat is a preserved heritage site honoring the arrival of Indian workers.

questions.prompt: In which year did Mauritius celebrate its independence?
questions.explain: Mauritius became an independent nation on March 12, 1968!

questions.prompt: What majestic mountain in Mauritius stands as a symbol of freedom and sanctuary?
questions.explain: Le Morne Brabant is a UNESCO site that symbolises hope, freedom, and resilience.

questions.prompt: Demographically, what is the largest religious community in Mauritius today?
questions.explain: Hinduism is practiced by nearly half of the population in Mauritius.

questions.prompt: Why is Mauritius lovingly nicknamed a "Rainbow Nation"?
options: Because of its flag colors only
Because of its harmonious mix of diverse cultures & traditions
questions.explain: Mauritius brings together Indian, African, European, and Chinese heritages in harmony!

questions.prompt: Who was the first Prime Minister of independent Mauritius, known as Father of the Nation?
questions.explain: Sir Seewoosagur Ramgoolam guided Mauritius into independence in 1968.
